ACCC appreciates this CMS effort to address ongoing concerns relating to prior authorization (PA) and to improve the 
use and interoperability of electronic records. ACCC welcomes the proposed ruleâ€™s extension of PA reforms to drugs for 
many types of plans, as well as many of its additional proposed requirements, as these changes have the potential to 
improve patient access to care and alleviate PA related administrative burdens on providers. While PA and related 
utilization management tools can serve legitimate purposes, such as supporting appropriate utilization and coverage 
determinations, these processes can create significant burdens on providers and patients with serious, chronic or 
complex conditions, such as cancer, and even result in negative clinical outcomes, if they are not designed or 
implemented in a manner that is timely and transparent, and takes clinical and medical realities into account.0F1
1F2 
 
ACCC respectfully offers the following comments on the proposed rule, focusing primarily on the provisions relating to 
required timeframes and processes relating to prior authorization (PA) decisions. 
 
â€¢ 
ACCC applauds CMSâ€™ proposed extension of required timeframes for PA decisions regarding drugs to several 
types of plans that were not previously subject to such standards, subject to the comments and suggestions 
contained herein.  
â€¢ 
ACCC additionally favors the new reporting requirements for PA decisions regarding drugs in the proposed rule 
as they will provide improved transparency to drug related PA processes. 
â€¢ 
ACCC supports the proposal to require that specified plans provide specific reasons for PA denials of requests 
relating to drugs. 
â€¢ 
ACCC favors the proposed ruleâ€™s interoperability requirements for many types of plans to support electronic PA 
of decisions relating to drugs.   
â€¢ 
ACCC also supports the proposed requirements relating to PA for non-drug services and drugs for QHPs on the 
FFEs. 
â€¢ 
ACCC does not support the proposal to allow QHPs to request extensions of PA timelines. 
â€¢ 
ACCC is in favor of the agencyâ€™s exploration of ways technology might help streamline step therapy and related 
utilization review mechanisms. 
â€¢ 
ACCC also responds to some CMS requests for input and suggests changes to certain proposed requirements, as 
detailed below.

1. New Standards for PA Decisions Relating to Drugs 
 
CMS proposes to extend certain protections to PA requests regarding drugs. It therefore builds upon the 2024 final rule 
that focused on â€œAdvancing Interoperability and Improving Prior Authorization Processesâ€ in Medicare Advantage 
plans; state Medicaid plans, both fee-for-service and managed care; Childrenâ€™s Health Insurance programs (CHIP), 
both fee-for-service (FFS) and managed care; and Qualified Health Plan (QHP) issuers, both individual and small 
group, on federally facilitated exchanges.2F3 
Under the proposal, qualified health plan insurers (QHPs) on the federally facilitated exchanges (FFEs) must notify the 
requesting provider about decisions on PA requests for drugs as expeditiously as required by the enrolleeâ€™s health 
condition, but no later than 72 hours after receiving a standard PA request and no later than 24 hours after receiving an 
expedited PA request. CMS also proposes to align the required timeline for CHIP FFS programs to respond to PA requests 
for drugs with the requirements that apply to Medicaid FFS programs and managed care plans and CHIP managed care 
plans. Under these requirements, such plans must respond to PA standard and expedited requests within 24 hours and 
dispense at least a 72-hour supply of the drug in the case of emergencies. ACCC supports these proposals. 
In addition, CMS requested input on whether they should shorten the proposed timelines for the decisions on drugs of 
QHPs on FFEs to align with the existing standards for State Medicaid FFS programs, Medicaid managed care plans, and 
Childrenâ€™s Health Insurance Program (CHIP) managed care entities, and its proposal for State CHIP FFS programs.  ACCC 
is in favor of the agency making this change to the proposed rule and believes aligned timelines for PA decisions on 
drugs among these programs would simplify PA administration for providers. 
2. Proposed Reporting Requirements Relating to PA Processes Relating to Drugs 
The proposed rule includes new PA-related reporting requirements for PA decisions relating to drugs for Medicare 
Advantage plans, qualified health plans (QHPs) on the federally facilitated exchanges (FFEs), and Medicaid and CHIP FFS 
and managed care plans. These new standards require public reporting on PA through new metrics related to denials 
and appeals, as well as additional information. ACCC supports these reporting requirements and believes they will add 
transparency to plan offerings and their PA processes and activities and potentially promote stronger PA oversight.  
3. Requirements for Improved Communications Between Plans and Providers Regarding the Reasons for Denials of PA 
Requests Relating to Drugs 
 
The proposal would require state Medicaid and CHIP FFS programs, Medicaid managed care plans, CHIP managed care 
entities, and QHP issuers on the FFEs to provide providers a specific reason for denying prior authorization requests for 
drugs. ACCC strongly supports this new requirement and believes it would improve plansâ€™ communications with 
providers and give providers important insights into plan decisions.  
 
4. Proposed Interoperability Requirements Relating to PA for Drugs to Promote Electronic PA Decisions 
The 2024 final rule relating to PA for non-drug decisions requires applicable payers to implement an electronic PA 
Application Programming Interface (API) as part of an effort to â€œreduce burdens on patients, providers, and payers.â€ 3F4 
Similarly, the proposed rule proposes interoperability standards for APIs to facilitate electronic prior authorization 
for drug decisions.  ACCC supports the movement towards electronic PA processes for drug-related PA decisions and 
believes it has the potential to reduce related administrative burdens.

5. New Required Timelines for QHPs on the Federally Facilitated Exchanges (FFEs) to Notify Providers of PA Decisions 
on Non-Drug Services and Decisions Relating to Drugs 
CMS also includes a proposal relating to PA for non-drug services and proposes that QHPs on the FFEs notify providers of 
their decision on a standard PA request for non-drug services as expeditiously as an enrolleeâ€™s health condition requires, 
but no later than 7 calendar days after receiving the request, and 72 hours after an expedited request. The latter is in 
line with requirements for notifying enrollees of determinations on expedited requests for non-drug services. The 
agency notes that these timelines are consistent with timeframes finalized for non-drug services in the 2024 CMS 
Interoperability and Prior Authorization final rule (hereinafter referred to as the â€œ2024 ruleâ€) for MA organizations, state 
Medicaid and CHIP FFS programs, Medicaid managed care plans, and CHIP managed care entities. 
The agency also proposes that QHPs on the FFEs must notify the requesting provider about decisions on PA requests for 
drugs as expeditiously as required by the enrolleeâ€™s health condition, but no later than 72 hours after receiving a 
standard PA request and no later than 24 hours after receiving an expedited PA request. The agency notes that these 
standards generally align with the requirements for Part D plans. As discussed in Section 1 of this letter, the agency also 
solicits input on shortening this standard to 24 hours for both standard and expedited PA requests for drugs, and ACCC 
would support such a change. 
ACCC supports the proposed timelines for PA decisions by QHPs on the FFEs for both non-drug services and drugs and 
asks the agency to implement the shorter, 24-hour timeframe for decisions relating to drugs for which it solicits input. 
ACCC also recognizes that applicable plans have already implemented, or are in the process of implementing, the 2024 
rule for PA decisions on non-drug services. That being said, ACCC favors the alignment of PA standards and timelines for 
requests for both non-drug and drug services to the maximum extent possible and requests that the agency consider the 
possibility of shorter, and possibly aligned, timeframes for decisions on drug and non-drug services in a future 
rulemaking. That being said, ACCC recognizes that there could be different considerations involved in PA decisions for 
non-drug services than for drug services. 
6. Allowing QHP issuers to request extensions of PA timeframes   
The proposed rule would allow QHPs issuers to extend the timeframes for notifying providers of a PA decision by up to 
14 calendar days under certain circumstances. QHPs would be required to provide providers with written notification of 
the reasons for the delay and inform providers of their right to file an expedited grievance.  ACCC does not support this 
proposal and believes it could undermine patientsâ€™ timely access to care and add additional administrative burdens on 
providers.  
7. Request for Information Relating to Step Therapy 
ACCC appreciates CMSâ€™ request for information (RFI) relating to step therapy, particularly the questions relating to 
whether increased interoperability of information technology systems across payers could help improve the 
transparency of utilization management processes, like step therapy, and how technology and data sharing might help 
streamline the step therapy process, such as by providing access to information about historical drug therapies that a 
patient may have already tried (such as when they change payers). ACCC supports improvements in step therapy 
processes, including changes that could avoid disruptions in therapy due to coverage transitions. ACCC would also 
support changes that could facilitate payersâ€™ access to, and ability to act upon, historical patient information, as well as 
those that would improve the transparency and efficiency of coverage processes for patients, providers, and payers.  
ACCC therefore supports CMSâ€™ exploration of ways technology can better support continuity and transitions of care and 
alleviate some of the burden and challenges of certain step therapy and related utilization review practices.

analysis:
## 1. COMMENTER INFORMATION

- **Author/Organization name:** Association of Cancer Care Centers (ACCC); signed by Meagan O'Neill, MS, Executive Director.
- **Stakeholder type:** Professional Association; Healthcare Provider/Advocacy Group.
- **Credentials or expertise mentioned:** ACCC describes itself as a cancer care education and advocacy organization with 50+ years of history, over 45,000 cancer care professionals, more than 1,700 member organizations, and representation of approximately two-thirds of U.S. oncology programs and practices.

## 2. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

ACCC supports extending prior authorization reforms to drugs, including required decision timeframes, denial reasons, reporting, and electronic PA interoperability, because these changes can improve cancer patient access and reduce provider burden. It asks CMS to shorten and align drug PA timelines where possible, reject QHP extensions of PA timeframes, and use technology to improve step therapy transparency and continuity across payer transitions.

## 3. REGULATORY CONTEXT

- **Specific provisions addressed:** PA-DRUG-MEDICAL; PA-DRUG-PHARMACY; PA-TIMEFRAMES-DRUGS; PA-DENIAL-REASONS; API-USAGE-METRICS; FHIR-IG-REQUIRED/electronic PA API generally; FF-SHOP-REQUIREMENTS/QHP requirements; GENERAL/RFI on step therapy.
- **Regulatory citations mentioned:** Federal Register citation 91 Fed. Reg. 19890; no CFR sections cited by number.
- **Standards referenced:** Electronic PA API; interoperability standards; information technology systems; no specific FHIR IG or NCPDP standard named.

## 4. DETAILED POSITIONS

**Topic 1: Drug prior authorization decision timeframes**
- **Provision ID:** PA-TIMEFRAMES-DRUGS
- **Position:** Support/Modify
- **Rationale:** ACCC supports extending required PA timeframes to drugs and states that timely decisions are particularly important for patients with serious, chronic, or complex conditions such as cancer.
- **Specific request:** Finalize proposed timeframes and shorten QHP FFE drug PA timelines to 24 hours for both standard and expedited requests if CMS chooses to align them with Medicaid/CHIP standards.

**Topic 2: Public reporting on drug PA processes**
- **Provision ID:** API-USAGE-METRICS; TRANSPARENCY/GENERAL
- **Position:** Support
- **Rationale:** ACCC says reporting on denials, appeals, and related PA metrics will add transparency to plan offerings and may strengthen oversight.
- **Specific request:** Finalize the new drug PA reporting requirements.

**Topic 3: Specific reasons for drug PA denials**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DENIAL-REASONS
- **Position:** Support
- **Rationale:** Specific denial reasons improve communication between plans and providers and give providers insight into plan decisions.
- **Specific request:** Require specified plans to provide providers a specific reason when denying drug PA requests.

**Topic 4: Electronic PA interoperability for drug decisions**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DRUG-MEDICAL; PA-DRUG-PHARMACY; FHIR-IG-REQUIRED
- **Position:** Support
- **Rationale:** ACCC believes electronic PA APIs and interoperability for drug decisions can reduce administrative burden.
- **Specific request:** Finalize interoperability requirements supporting electronic PA decisions for drugs.

**Topic 5: QHP FFE PA timelines and extension requests**
- **Provision ID:** FF-SHOP-REQUIREMENTS; PA-TIMEFRAMES-DRUGS
- **Position:** Support proposed timelines; Oppose extensions
- **Rationale:** ACCC supports QHP FFE decision timelines for non-drug services and drugs but says 14-day extensions could undermine timely access and add administrative burden.
- **Specific request:** Implement proposed QHP FFE PA timelines, consider shorter aligned timeframes in future rulemaking, and do not allow QHP issuers to extend PA decision timeframes by up to 14 calendar days.

**Topic 6: Step therapy and technology**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Support/Clarify
- **Rationale:** ACCC supports technology and data sharing that can improve transparency, continuity, and transition of care, including access to historical drug therapy information when patients change payers.
- **Specific request:** Continue exploring ways technology can streamline step therapy and related utilization review and avoid therapy disruptions during coverage transitions.

## 5. SOLICITATION RESPONSES

- **S16-S17:** Supports requiring specific reasons for drug PA denials because it improves plan-provider communication and provider understanding of decisions.
- **S20/S43:** Supports proposed drug PA timeframes and favors shortening QHP FFE drug decisions to 24 hours for both standard and expedited requests to align with Medicaid/CHIP programs.
- **S21:** Supports applying required timeframes to drugs, especially for serious and complex conditions such as cancer, while requesting stronger alignment and shorter timelines.
- **S29-S30/S34-S35:** Supports reporting requirements for drug PA denials, appeals, and other metrics to improve transparency and oversight.
- **S40-S42:** Supports QHP FFE PA requirements for non-drug services and drugs, but opposes allowing QHPs to request 14-day extensions of PA timeframes.
- **S66-S82:** Responds to the RFI on step therapy by supporting technology, interoperability, and data sharing to improve transparency, continuity, and transitions of care.

## 6. RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Finalize required PA decision timeframes for drugs across affected plans.
2. Shorten QHP FFE drug PA decision timelines to 24 hours for both standard and expedited requests.
3. Align PA standards and timelines for drug and non-drug services as much as possible, including in future rulemaking where needed.
4. Finalize public reporting requirements for drug PA denials, appeals, and related process metrics.
5. Require specific denial reasons for drug PA requests.
6. Finalize electronic PA interoperability requirements for drug decisions.
7. Do not allow QHP issuers to extend PA decision timeframes by up to 14 days.
8. Use technology and data sharing to improve step therapy transparency and continuity during payer transitions.

## 7. CONCERNS & OBJECTIONS

- **Primary concerns:** PA delays and administrative burden for patients and providers in cancer care; insufficient transparency; QHP extension requests that could delay care; step therapy disruption during coverage transitions.
- **Potential negative impacts cited:** Negative clinical outcomes for patients with serious, chronic, or complex conditions; undermined timely access to care; additional provider administrative burdens; disruptions in therapy when patients change payers.
- **Implementation barriers mentioned:** Variation in timelines across programs, lack of transparency in denials and appeals, potential QHP delays, and incomplete access to historical therapy information for step therapy decisions.

## 8. SUPPORTING EVIDENCE

- **Data or statistics cited:** ACCC has over 45,000 cancer care professional members, more than 1,700 member organizations, and represents approximately two-thirds of U.S. oncology programs and practices.
- **Studies or research referenced:** National Health Council report on prior authorization burden for patients with chronic disease; 2025 AMA Prior Authorization Physician Survey; Health Affairs Forefront article by Kyle and Sachs on CMS's proposed rule.
- **Examples provided:** Cancer care as a serious, chronic, and complex care context where delayed or opaque PA can affect clinical outcomes; step therapy disruptions when patients change payers.

## 9. IMPACT ASSESSMENT

- **Affected stakeholders:** Cancer patients, oncology providers and care teams, QHP issuers on FFEs, Medicaid and CHIP programs, MA plans, payers, CMS, and providers handling PA and appeals.
- **Economic implications:** The comment does not quantify financial costs but links PA burden to provider administrative workload and implies that transparency and electronic PA can reduce administrative burden.
- **Technical feasibility:** ACCC supports electronic PA APIs and interoperability as feasible tools to streamline drug PA and step therapy if implemented with timely and transparent processes.
- **Patient care impact:** Faster, transparent PA decisions are important to prevent delays and negative outcomes for cancer patients and others with serious or complex conditions.

## 10. SENTIMENT ANALYSIS

- **Overall position:** Supportive with targeted objections
- **Tone:** Professional, collaborative, and patient-access focused
- **Priority level:** High

## 11. KEY QUOTES

1. "ACCC welcomes the proposed rule's extension of PA reforms to drugs" - Context: Overall support for applying reforms to drug PA.
2. "ACCC strongly supports this new requirement" - Context: Support for specific denial reasons.
3. "ACCC does not support this proposal" - Context: Opposition to allowing QHP issuers to extend PA timeframes.
4. "avoid disruptions in therapy due to coverage transitions" - Context: Step therapy and technology RFI response.

## 12. THEMES

- [x] **IMPLEMENTATION-TIMELINE** - ACCC focuses heavily on PA decision timeframes, shorter deadlines, and opposition to extensions.
- [x] **PROVIDER-BURDEN** - The comment emphasizes administrative burden on oncology providers and care teams.
- [x] **TECHNICAL-FEASIBILITY** - ACCC supports electronic PA APIs, interoperability, and technology-enabled step therapy improvements.
- [x] **PATIENT-ACCESS** - The comment centers on timely access for cancer patients and others with serious or complex conditions.
- [x] **STAKEHOLDER-COORDINATION** - Recommendations involve CMS, QHPs, Medicaid/CHIP programs, MA plans, oncology providers, and payers sharing historical therapy data.
- [x] **TRANSPARENCY** - ACCC supports reporting requirements and specific denial reasons to improve visibility into PA processes.
- [x] **FF-SHOP-REQUIREMENTS** - The comment supports QHP FFE PA requirements for non-drug and drug services and opposes extension allowances.
- [x] **EXISTING-WORKFLOWS** - It addresses PA communications, appeals, step therapy processes, and continuity during payer transitions.
